comment: The call sites of the runtime entries, census row E48 of notes/compiler.md 9. A call takes its
name and its result from the row of rt_sig_of in src/fort/runtime_sig.ft, and each call site
writes its arguments; rt_call_check of src/fort/gen.ft panics when the count or the form of an
argument, or the type of a named result, differs from the row. Rows E48-call-* change the type
of one argument or of one result at a call site: the line of the location, the size of `alloc`,
the count of `args_init`, the sign flag of `regrow` and the result of `alloc`. Row
E48-call-check-removed removes the panic. The first stage runs 5 suites of test/fort, and the
pinned compiler bootstrap-2 builds them: each suite compiles the mutated gen.ft and fir_llvm.ft
from source, but the compiler is no mutant. The suites lower each mutated call site in the
process of the test: gen_ir_test (the location), fir_llvm_call_test (`alloc`, `args_init`),
gen_function_test (`args_init`), fir_llvm_regrow_test (`regrow`) and the panic test of
rt_call_check. So rt_call_check panics when the test runs, and run_tests.py prints a `FAIL`
line; with the removed panic, the panic test exits 0 and fails. A mutant compiler panics while
it compiles a test, which run_tests.py reports as ERROR and no failed test. The first stage
needs the bootstrap chain (FORT_ENABLE_BOOTSTRAP0) and the standard root that the chain
assembles for HEAD. The build fails when the pinned compiler is absent, so the run stops with
"the baseline does not build" and catches no row. The second stage runs the same suites with
the mutant compiler, and the third the programs of test/lang whose name holds `regrow`. The
table runs on a darwin host with --runner 'bash -c'; ZERO_AR_DATE=1 keeps the md5 guard. The
md5 guard reads the product compiler that the build links.

stages.name: the emitter suites, built by the last pinned compiler
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Darwin/debug/bootstrap/bootstrap-2/fort --std-dir build/Darwin/debug/bootstrap/head/std --cc /opt/homebrew/bin/clang --target arm64-apple-macosx11.0.0 --timeout 1500 -v -j 6 gen_rt_call_check fir_llvm_regrow_test gen_ir_test fir_llvm_call_test gen_function_test

stages.name: the emitter suites
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Darwin/debug/fort --std-dir build/Darwin/debug/std --cc /opt/homebrew/bin/clang --target arm64-apple-macosx11.0.0 --opt /opt/homebrew/bin/opt --verify-ir -v -j 10 gen_rt_call_check fir_llvm_regrow_test gen_ir_test fir_llvm_call_test gen_function_test

stages.name: the regrow programs
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Darwin/debug/fort --std-dir build/Darwin/debug/std --cc /opt/homebrew/bin/clang --target arm64-apple-macosx11.0.0 --opt /opt/homebrew/bin/opt --verify-ir -j 10 --xfail test/lang/xfail.txt regrow

mutations.what: the line of each location is an i64, and each row gives i32
the size of an element of `alloc` is an i32, and the row gives i64
the count of the arguments of `args_init` is an i64, and the row gives i32
the sign flag of `regrow` is an i8, and the row gives `i1 zeroext`
the result of `alloc` is named as an i64, and the row gives ptr
rt_call_check lets a call that differs from its row pass
